The method performs a single Act (g.insereAresta(...)) and then a single coherent set of assertions verifying the result and side effects. There is one Arrange-Act-Assert flow.

The test uses only local variables and helper calls (newGraph(), assertDefaultGraphInvariant()) and does not rely on shared mutable state visible in the method. No evidence of ordered test naming or shared mutable fields in the method.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: Only a single happy-path test is present. There is no test for error/exceptional conditions (e.g., invalid vertex indices) and the class contains fewer than two test methods, so exceptional flows are not covered.
The test uses typical values (0 and 1748) and does not exercise boundary conditions such as negative indices or maximum vertex index. No explicit boundary checks are present.
The test leverages helper methods (newGraph(), assertDefaultGraphInvariant()) from the scaffolding, indicating modular setup and reuse rather than duplicating setup logic.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: The method is short (<20 lines), linear, contains no loops or complex conditionals and follows a clear Arrange-Act-Assert pattern.
The test contains multiple targeted assertions: existence of the inserted edge, non-existence of an unrelated edge, and vertex count verification—verifying several properties to detect faults.
No @Ignore/@Disabled annotations or commented-out @Test methods are present in the provided snippet. The test is active and runnable.
Class Javadoc explicitly references a requirement (REQ-GRAPH-1), providing traceability from tests to requirement IDs.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: No performance or security tests are expected in a unit test. The method contains no explicit performance/security checks (timeouts are used for test runtime but not for performance assertions).
The test method name 'test6' is generic and does not describe the scenario or expected outcome. It does not follow descriptive naming conventions.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: The test class uses EvoSuite runtime annotations (EvoRunner, EvoRunnerParameters) and the test method has a generated-style name 'test6', which are signs of heavy test generation rather than minimal, intention-revealing tests.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: The class-level Javadoc and method comments indicate Given-When-Then style and the assertions are descriptive, showing evidence of a considered design approach.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test exercises public API methods only (newGraph(), insereAresta, existeAresta, numVertices) and does not access private internals or use reflection, indicating behavior-focused, maintainable tests.
Assertions include descriptive failure messages and use specific assertion methods (assertTrue/assertFalse/assertEquals) rather than overly-generic assertions. Messages improve diagnosability.
The class contains useful Javadoc linking to requirements and the method includes minimal Given/When/Then comments. There is no excessive or commented-out code in the provided snippet.
The test contains no sources of non-determinism (no random, time-based calls, no Thread.sleep) and uses local state; the EvoRunner configuration is present but the test logic itself is deterministic.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: The test modifies only local graph instance state and does not persist external resources. No file/database operations or static state modifications are visible in the method.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: The class is annotated with @Category(GraphUnitTest.class), enabling selective execution of the test group.

The test performs multiple distinct checks on the newly created graph: it asserts the vertex count equals NUM_VERTICES, asserts the count is > 0, and asserts an arbitrary edge does not exist. These represent multiple verification concerns (count correctness and edge absence) and multiple 'Act' operations (calls to numVertices() and existeAresta()), so the test is not atomic.

The test uses only local variables (local Grafo g) and does not reference or modify shared static/instance mutable state within the method. No ordering hints or numeric method names are present. Although no @Before/@After appear in the snippet, the method is self-contained and does not share mutable state.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: Only a single happy-path test exists in the provided class snippet. There is no test for error conditions or exceptional flows (e.g., invalid indices or null inputs). According to the evaluation rules, the class provides only happy-path coverage and lacks tests for error scenarios.

The test only checks an arbitrary pair of vertex indices (0 and 1) and the documented default vertex count; it does not exercise boundary values (e.g., negative index, zero boundary, last valid index, index equal to NUM_VERTICES) that are important for index-based graph APIs.
The test is short and self-contained (< 15 lines) and does not duplicate code within the shown snippet. Given the single test, there is no repeated setup that would mandate helper extraction.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: The test method is small (well under 20-30 lines), linear, and contains no loops or complex conditionals, giving it low cyclomatic complexity.

The test asserts multiple properties of the new graph (vertex count equals documented value, count > 0, and absence of an arbitrary edge). These multiple checks increase the chance of detecting faults in the graph initialization.
No @Ignore/@Disabled annotations are present in the shown snippet and there are no commented-out test methods. The test is active and runnable (it has @Test and a timeout).
The class Javadoc includes a requirement reference '(REQ-GRAPH-1)', providing traceability from the tests to a documented requirement.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: This is a unit test focused on functional behavior. No explicit performance or security tests are present. The presence of a timeout annotation does not indicate a dedicated performance or security test, so this practice is not applicable here.
The test method name 'test7' is generic and does not describe the scenario or expected outcome. It fails to follow descriptive naming conventions that communicate the test intent.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: The test class is run with EvoRunner and EvoRunnerParameters and uses a generated-style test name 'test7', which are strong signals of heavy test-generation tool use. The presence of such generated artifacts suggests code generation produced the test and the test name is not intention-revealing.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: The test includes 'Given & When' and 'Then' comments (BDD-style) and the class Javadoc claims Given-When-Then style and descriptive assertion messages, indicating some design intent rather than purely ad-hoc tests.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test interacts with the Grafo public API (numVertices, existeAresta) without using reflection or accessing private internals. It verifies observable behavior through public methods.
Assertions are specific (assertEquals, assertTrue, assertFalse) and include descriptive failure messages, which aid diagnosis of failures and are preferred over generic assertions.
Comments are minimal and explain the test structure ('Given & When', 'Then') rather than restating obvious code. No commented-out code is present in the shown snippet.
The test contains no sources of non-determinism such as Random, current time usage, Thread.sleep, or external dependencies. It operates deterministically on a freshly created graph object.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: The test uses only local variables and does not create files, modify static variables, or persist data. No cleanup is necessary for the operations shown.
